questions.prompt: The general led three legions across the river within five days.
questions.answer: Dux trēs legiōnēs trāns flūmen quīnque diēbus dūxit.

questions.prompt: Twelve captives, bound with chains, were dragged into the forum.
questions.answer: Duodecim captīvī, catēnīs vīnctī, in forum tractī sunt.

questions.prompt: Twenty ships, driven by a fierce wind, perished near the rocks.
questions.answer: Vīgintī nāvēs, ācrī ventō āctae, prope saxa periērunt.

questions.prompt: With eight horsemen the scout returned before dawn.
questions.answer: Cum octō equitibus explōrātor ante lūcem rediit.

questions.prompt: On the fourth day the exhausted soldiers finally reached the sea.
questions.answer: Quārtō diē mīlitēs fessī tandem mare attigērunt.

questions.prompt: The tenth legion, famous for its courage, held the right wing.
questions.answer: Legiō decima, virtūte clāra, dextrum cornū tenuit.

questions.prompt: In the first watch the enemy attacked the sleeping camp.
questions.answer: Prīmā vigiliā hostēs dormientia castra oppugnāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The second consul, having been recalled, entrusted the army to his colleague.
questions.answer: Secundus cōnsul, revocātus, exercitum collēgae mandāvit.

questions.prompt: The prisoners were led out two by two through the narrow gate.
questions.answer: Captīvī bīnī per angustam portam ēductī sunt.

questions.prompt: The general gave each soldier ten denarii before the battle.
questions.answer: Imperātor singulīs mīlitibus dēnōs dēnāriōs ante proelium dedit.

questions.prompt: The maidens, singing sweetly, entered the temple one by one.
questions.answer: Virginēs, suāviter canentēs, singulae templum intrāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Three by three the weary travelers crossed the swollen stream.
questions.answer: Ternī fessī viātōrēs tumidum rīvum trānsiērunt.

questions.prompt: The old man had seen Rome only once in his long life.
questions.answer: Senex Rōmam semel tantum in longā vītā vīderat.

questions.prompt: Twice the enemy attacked the walls, and twice they were repelled.
questions.answer: Bis hostēs mūrōs oppugnāvērunt, et bis repulsī sunt.

questions.prompt: The priest performed the sacred rites three times before the altar.
questions.answer: Sacerdōs ter sacra ante āram fēcit.

questions.prompt: Four times the messenger, exhausted, had crossed the mountains.
questions.answer: Quater nūntius, fessus, montēs trānscenderat.

questions.prompt: In the thirtieth year of his reign the king built a splendid temple.
questions.answer: Trīcēsimō rēgnī annō rēx splendidum templum aedificāvit.

questions.prompt: The wall, forty feet high, protected the ancient city.
questions.answer: Mūrus, quadrāgintā pedēs altus, urbem antīquam mūniēbat.

questions.prompt: The two sisters, joined by great love, lived in a small house.
questions.answer: Duae sorōrēs, magnō amōre iūnctae, in parvā domō habitābant.

questions.prompt: A thousand soldiers guarded the bridge throughout the night.
questions.answer: Mīlle mīlitēs pontem tōtā nocte custōdiēbant.

questions.prompt: Since the seven hills were sacred, the Romans set up altars there.
questions.answer: Cum septem collēs sacrī essent, Rōmānī ibi ārās posuērunt.

questions.prompt: The sixth cohort, placed on the hill, watched the approaching enemy.
questions.answer: Sexta cohors, in colle collocāta, hostēs appropinquantēs spectābat.

questions.prompt: For nine years the war raged before the city was captured.
questions.answer: Novem annōs bellum saeviit antequam urbs capta est.

questions.prompt: The eighteenth soldier in the line carried the sacred standard.
questions.answer: Duodēvīcēsimus mīles in ōrdine sacrum signum ferēbat.
